subject: Dedicated allocator ops matrix review
messages:
From: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Dedicated allocator ops matrix review

Team —

I pulled an updated allocator matrix (attached) and sketched a short set of asks for cross-functional alignment on the Nimbus Labs pilot next quarter. High level: Nimbus is asking for a temporary 20% headroom carve (pilot lanes) for a 6-week window to validate low-latency routing, and they want an autoscale-exception window during the ramp. Before committing anything we need ops confirmation on safety, product sign-off on prioritization, and legal/finance to be looped for any contract changes.

Quick asks:
- Marcus: validate whether the allocator can enforce a soft headroom + automatic fallback to a lower-cost pool when utilization crosses 95%. If not, what telemetry gaps block that?
- Kimberly: product needs to understand how this exception impacts other pilots (priority lanes) and whether we can gate it to request patterns (prefix caching heavy).
- Laura: ops runbook updates and exact calendar window proposal — can you propose one?
- Neha: I'll need a short note about whether we should treat this as a committed reservation (billable) vs courtesy headroom during evaluation.

Attached: allocator-matrix-v2.xlsx (matrix + proposed mappings). I created a lightweight policy draft (proposed-temporary-allocator-policy.md) — not attached here to reduce noise, will share next. Can we aim to close decisions by end-of-day Thu (Dec 9)? Nimbus is targeting an onboarding date of Jan 10, 2027.

Thanks,
Jonas
Jonas Weber
Head of Product Operations, Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 07 Dec 2026 11:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated allocator ops matrix review

Jonas — thanks for the summary and for pulling the matrix. I skimmed the sheet and added a couple of inline notes (high-level: the proposed headroom mapping looks reasonable but we need tighter SLAs on canary rollback).

A couple of clarifying questions:
- When you say "autoscale-exception window" do you mean a temporary raise of the max-instances parameter, or an intentional suppression of autoscale downscales for the pilot? Those have different risk profiles for preemptible capacity.
- Do we limit the exception to requests that match a set of known prefixes (Nimbus uses heavy prompt prefixing) so we avoid giving headroom to noisy exploratory workloads?

Operationally, if we go the "suppress downscale" route I want to see a fail-open fallback that routes to the shared burst pool with token-based throttling. I attached a short SLA exhibits draft (pilot-sla-exhibits.pdf) that spells expected latency and a simple rollback clause.

I can join a 30-minute alignment call if Marcus wants to walk the allocator constraints.

-Kimberly
Kimberly Park
Director, Product — Capacity & Reliability
Redwood Inference

From: Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 08 Dec 2026 14:22:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated allocator ops matrix review

Thanks — I reviewed the matrix and ran a short feasibility check with infra. Short answer: we can implement a soft headroom carve with an automated fallback but there are two caveats:

1) Telemetry: we need latency-percentile breakdown per allocator partition to decide the 95% cutoff reliably. Current metrics give pool-level utilization but not allocator-partition p95/p99 per model variant. That requires a small metrics instrumenting change (adds ~4% cardinality to our metrics pipeline).

2) Preemptible behavior: for burst fallback we can route to preemptible instances, but the risk is increased cold-starts for cold KV caches — that will affect p95. We can mitigate with a short warm-up window and a KV-prefetch pass but that will cost tokens and complexity.

Proposal:
- Short term (pilot): grant requested 20% headroom for Nimbus on a single partition and enforce a strict request-prefix whitelist. We enable autoscale suppression (no scale-down) only for those whitelisted prefixes and for a bounded window (Dec 28 — Jan 15). We add a phased telemetry change to deliver p95/p99 by Dec 20.
- Long term: add allocator-level p95/p99 to our standard SLI set and build a runbook that migrates traffic to burst pools when signals cross thresholds.

I can own the telemetry change and the fallback routing playbook with ops help. If we need to accept the small cardinality cost, we should document the tradeoff for finance.

-Marcus
Marcus Lin
Principal Systems Engineer, Serving Runtime
Redwood Inference

From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas.weber@redwood.ai>, Marcus Lin <marcus.lin@redwood.ai>, Kimberly Park <kimberly.park@redwood.ai>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.ai>, sarah@nimbus-labs.com
Date: Thu, 09 Dec 2026 16:40:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Dedicated allocator ops matrix review

Team —

Appreciate the fast turnaround. After syncing with Ops and Finance, here's a pragmatic decision and action plan that should keep us safe while supporting the Nimbus pilot:

Decision summary (agreed):
- Approve temporary 20% headroom on a single dedicated partition for Nimbus Labs for the window Dec 28, 2026 — Jan 15, 2027.
- Autoscale behavior: suppress scale-downs for whitelisted prefixes only. If partition utilization >= 95% for more than 3 consecutive minutes, route overflow to the shared burst pool with token-throttling.
- Telemetry requirement: Marcus to deliver p95/p99 allocator-partition metrics by Dec 20. This is a gating item for pilot start.
- Billing: treat the window as a billable temporary reservation (Neha to confirm SOW addendum).

Action items:
- Marcus: add allocator-partition p95/p99 metrics + run a short simulation by Dec 18 (owns).
- Kimberly: finalize the whitelist criteria and SLA rollback clause; publish pilot-sla-exhibits.pdf to the Nimbus folder and confirm with PM by Dec 12 (owns).
- Neha: draft SOW addendum language treating this as a billable temporary reservation and circulate for legal review by Dec 14 (owns).
- Jonas: coordinate final sign-off with Nimbus PM and schedule a 30-minute go/no-go on Dec 21 (owns).
- Ops: update runbook with the fallback routing behavior and test failover by Dec 22 (ops owns).

I've attached a short decision summary (decision-summary-nimbus.txt) and the final proposed policy doc (proposed-temporary-allocator-policy.md).

Sarah (Nimbus) — I'm CCing you so you have visibility. If you see any blocker on your side for the Dec 28 start, tell us now so we can adjust the window.

We'll treat this as an exception with a clearly bounded scope and a telemetry gating condition. If anyone objects to the plan above, flag it in the next 12 hours and we'll escalate.

Thanks,
Laura
Laura Bennett
VP, Technical Operations
Redwood Inference
